The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:1.

And the LORD spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

Καὶ ἐλάλησεν Κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν λέγων καὶ Ἀαρών

Douay-Rheims

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

JPS (1917)

And the LORD spoke unto Moses and to Aaron, saying:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, dicens:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَكَلَّمَ ٱلرَّبُّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ قَائِلًا:

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:2.

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When any man hath a running issue out of his flesh, [because of] his issue he [is] unclean.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

דַּבְּרוּ֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אִ֗ישׁ כִּ֤י יִהְיֶה֙ זָ֣ב מִבְּשָׂר֔וֹ זוֹב֖וֹ טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

Λάλησον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἐρεῖς αὐτοῖς Ἀνδρὶ ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ἐὰν γένηται ῥύσις ἐκ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ, ἡ ῥύσις αὐτοῦ ἀκάθαρτός ἐστιν.

Douay-Rheims

Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: The man that hath an issue of seed, shall be unclean.

JPS (1917)

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them: When any man hath an issue out of his flesh, his issue is unclean.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Loquimini filiis Israël, et dicite eis: Vir, qui patitur fluxum seminis, immundus erit.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

«كَلِّمَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَقُولَا لَهُمْ: كُلُّ رَجُلٍ يَكُونُ لَهُ سَيْلٌ مِنْ لَحْمِهِ، فَسَيْلُهُ نَجِسٌ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:3.

And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue: whether his flesh run with his issue, or his flesh be stopped from his issue, it [is] his uncleanness.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְזֹ֛את תִּהְיֶ֥ה טֻמְאָת֖וֹ בְּזוֹב֑וֹ רָ֣ר בְּשָׂר֞וֹ אֶת־זוֹב֗וֹ אֽוֹ־הֶחְתִּ֤ים בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ מִזּוֹב֔וֹ טֻמְאָת֖וֹ הִֽוא׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

καὶ οὗτος ὁ νόμος τῆς ἀκαθαρσίας αὐτοῦ· ῥέων γόνον ἐκ σώματος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῆς ῥύσεως ἧς συνέστηκεν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ διὰ τῆς ῥύσεως, αὕτη ἡ ἀκαθαρσία αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ· πᾶσαι αἱ ἡμέραι ῥύσεως σώματος αὐτοῦ ᾗ συνέστηκεν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ διὰ τῆς ῥύσεως ἀκαθαρσία αὐτοῦ ἐστίν.

Douay-Rheims

And then shall he be judged subject to this evil, when a filthy humour, at every moment, cleaveth to his flesh, and gathereth there.

JPS (1917)

And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue: whether his flesh run with his issue, or his flesh be stopped from his issue, it is his uncleanness.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Et tunc judicabitur huic vitio subjacere, cum per singula momenta adhæserit carni ejus, atque concreverit fœdus humor.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَهَذِهِ تَكُونُ نَجَاسَتُهُ بِسَيْلِهِ: إِنْ كَانَ لَحْمُهُ يَبْصُقُ سَيْلَهُ، أَوْ يَحْتَبِسُ لَحْمُهُ عَنْ سَيْلِهِ، فَذَلِكَ نَجَاسَتُهُ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:4.

Every bed, whereon he lieth that hath the issue, is unclean: and every thing, whereon he sitteth, shall be unclean.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

כָּל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכַּ֥ב עָלָ֛יו הַזָּ֖ב יִטְמָ֑א וְכָֽל־הַכְּלִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־יֵשֵׁ֥ב עָלָ֖יו יִטְמָֽא׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

πᾶσα κοίτη ἐφ᾽ ᾗ ἐὰν κοιμηθῇ ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς ὁ γονορρυὴς ἀκάθαρτός ἐστιν, καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐφ᾽ ὃ ἐὰν καθίσῃ ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸ ὁ γονορρυὴς ἀκάθαρτον ἔσται.

Douay-Rheims

Every bed on which he sleepeth, shall be unclean, and every place on which he sitteth.

JPS (1917)

Every bed whereon he that hath the issue lieth shall be unclean; and every thing whereon he sitteth shall be unclean.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Omne stratum, in quo dormierit, immundum erit, et ubicumque sederit.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

كُلُّ فِرَاشٍ يَضْطَجِعُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُ ٱلسَّيْلُ يَكُونُ نَجِسًا، وَكُلُّ مَتَاعٍ يَجْلِسُ عَلَيْهِ يَكُونُ نَجِسًا.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:5.

And whosoever toucheth his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִגַּ֖ע בְּמִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

καὶ ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἄν ἅψηται τῆς κοίτης αὐτοῦ πλυνεῖ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ λούσεται ὕδατι, καὶ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας·

Douay-Rheims

If ally man touch his bed, he shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.

JPS (1917)

And whosoever toucheth his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Si quis hominum tetigerit lectum ejus, lavabit vestimenta sua, et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَمَنْ مَسَّ فِرَاشَهُ يَغْسِلُ ثِيَابَهُ وَيَسْتَحِمُّ بِمَاءٍ، وَيَكُونُ نَجِسًا إِلَى ٱلْمَسَاءِ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:6.

And he that sitteth on [any] thing whereon he sat that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְהַיֹּשֵׁב֙ עַֽל־הַכְּלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־יֵשֵׁ֥ב עָלָ֖יו הַזָּ֑ב יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ σκεύους ἐφ᾽ ὃ ἐὰν καθίσῃ ὁ γονορρυὴς πλυνεῖ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ λούσεται ὕδατι, καὶ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας.

Douay-Rheims

If a man sit where that man hath sitten, he also shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.

JPS (1917)

And he that sitteth on any thing whereon he that hath the issue sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Si sederit ubi ille sederat, et ipse lavabit vestimenta sua: et lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَمَنْ جَلَسَ عَلَى ٱلْمَتَاعِ ٱلَّذِي يَجْلِسُ عَلَيْهِ ذُو ٱلسَّيْلِ، يَغْسِلُ ثِيَابَهُ وَيَسْتَحِمُّ بِمَاءٍ، وَيَكُونُ نَجِسًا إِلَى ٱلْمَسَاءِ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:7.

And he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְהַנֹּגֵ֖עַ בִּבְשַׂ֣ר הַזָּ֑ב יְכַבֵּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

καὶ ὁ ἁπτόμενος χρωτὸς τοῦ γονορρυοῦς πλυνεῖ τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ λούσεται ὕδατι, καὶ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας·

Douay-Rheims

He that toucheth his flesh, shall wash his clothes: and being himself washed with water shall be unclean until the evening.

JPS (1917)

And he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Qui tetigerit carnem ejus, lavabit vestimenta sua: et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَمَنْ مَسَّ لَحْمَ ذِي ٱلسَّيْلِ يَغْسِلُ ثِيَابَهُ وَيَسْتَحِمُّ بِمَاءٍ، وَيَكُونُ نَجِسًا إِلَى ٱلْمَسَاءِ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:8.

And if he that hath the issue spit upon him that is clean; then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְכִֽי־יָרֹ֛ק הַזָּ֖ב בַּטָּה֑וֹר וְכִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

ἐὰν δὲ προσσιελίσῃ ὁ γονορρυὴς ἐπὶ τὸν καθαρὸν, πλυνεῖ τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ λούσεται ὕδατι, καὶ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας·

Douay-Rheims

If such a man cast his spittle upon him that is clean, he shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.

JPS (1917)

And if he that hath the issue spit upon him that is clean, then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Si salivam hujuscemodi homo jecerit super eum qui mundus est, lavabit vestimenta sua: et lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَإِنْ بَصَقَ ذُو ٱلسَّيْلِ عَلَى طَاهِرٍ، يَغْسِلُ ثِيَابَهُ وَيَسْتَحِمُّ بِمَاءٍ، وَيَكُونُ نَجِسًا إِلَى ٱلْمَسَاءِ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:9.

And what saddle soever he rideth upon that hath the issue shall be unclean.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְכָל־הַמֶּרְכָּ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְכַּ֥ב עָלָ֛יו הַזָּ֖ב יִטְמָֽא׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

καὶ πᾶν ἐπίσαγμα ὄνου ἐφ᾽ ὃ ἂν ἐπιβῇ ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸ ὁ γονορρυής, ἀκάθαρτον ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας.

Douay-Rheims

The saddle on which he hath sitten shall be unclean.

JPS (1917)

And what saddle soever he that hath the issue rideth upon shall be unclean.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Sagma, super quo sederit, immundum erit:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَكُلُّ مَا يَرْكَبُ عَلَيْهِ ذُو ٱلسَّيْلِ يَكُونُ نَجِسًا.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 15:10.

ponam faciem meam super hominem illum, et super cognationem ejus, succidamque et ipsum, et omnes qui consenserunt ei ut fornicarentur cum Moloch, de medio populi sui.

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:9.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

כִּֽי־אִ֣ישׁ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְקַלֵּ֧ל אֶת־אָבִ֛יו וְאֶת־אִמּ֖וֹ מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֑ת אָבִ֧יו וְאִמּ֛וֹ קִלֵּ֖ל דָּמָ֥יו בּֽוֹ׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

ἄνθρωπος ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἂν κακῶς εἴπῃ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ ἢ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ θανάτῳ θανατούσθω· πατέρα αὐτοῦ ἢ μητέρα αὐτοῦ κακῶς εἶπεν, ἔνοχος ἔσται.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:10.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:11.

And if a man shall take his sister, his father’s daughter, or his mother’s daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness; it [is] a wicked thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of their people: he hath uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

And if a man shall take his sister, his father's daughter, or his mother's daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness: it is a shameful thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of the children of their people: he hath uncovered his sister's nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Qui acceperit sororem suam filiam patris sui, vel filiam matris suæ, et viderit turpitudinem ejus, illaque conspexerit fratris ignominiam, nefariam rem operati sunt: occidentur in conspectu populi sui, eo quod turpitudinem suam mutuo revelaverint, et portabunt iniquitatem suam.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَإِذَا أَخَذَ رَجُلٌ أُخْتَهُ بِنْتَ أَبِيهِ أَوْ بِنْتَ أُمِّهِ، وَرَأَى عَوْرَتَهَا وَرَأَتْ هِيَ عَوْرَتَهُ، فَذَلِكَ عَارٌ. يُقْطَعَانِ أَمَامَ أَعْيُنِ بَنِي شَعْبِهِمَا. قَدْ كَشَفَ عَوْرَةَ أُخْتِهِ. يَحْمِلُ ذَنْبَهُ.

↩

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:18.

And if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness, and shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

וְ֠אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִשְׁכַּ֨ב אֶת־אִשָּׁ֜ה דָּוָ֗ה וְגִלָּ֤ה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָהּ֙ אֶת־מְקֹרָ֣הּ הֶֽעֱרָ֔ה וְהִ֕יא גִּלְּתָ֖ה אֶת־מְק֣וֹר דָּמֶ֑יהָ וְנִכְרְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽם׃

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

καὶ ἀνὴρ ὃς ἂν κοιμηθῇ μετὰ γυναικὸς ἀποκαθημένης καὶ ἀποκαλύψῃ τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτῆς, τὴν πηγὴν αὐτῆς ἀπεκάλυψεν, καὶ αὕτη ἀπεκάλυψεν τὴν ῥύσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς· ἐξολεθρευθήσονται ἀμφότεροι ἐκ τοῦ γένους αὐτῶν.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Qui coierit cum muliere in fluxu menstruo, et revelaverit turpitudinem ejus, ipsaque aperuerit fontem sanguinis sui, interficientur ambo de medio populi sui.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَإِذَا ٱضْطَجَعَ رَجُلٌ مَعَ ٱمْرَأَةٍ طَامِثٍ وَكَشَفَ عَوْرَتَهَا، عَرَّى يَنْبُوعَهَا وَكَشَفَتْ هِيَ يَنْبُوعَ دَمِهَا، يُقْطَعَانِ كِلَاهُمَا مِنْ شَعِبْهِمَا.

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:19.

And thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister, nor of thy father’s sister: for he uncovereth his near kin: they shall bear their iniquity.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:20.

Greek (Septuagint / Swete)

Douay-Rheims

If any mall lie with the wife of his uncle by the father, or of his uncle by the mother, and uncover the shame of his near akin, both shall bear their sin: they shall die without children.

JPS (1917)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:21.

And if a man shall take his brother’s wife, it [is] an unclean thing: he hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they shall be childless.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)

JPS (1917)

The Third Book of Moses, Leviticus 20:22.

Hebrew (Masoretic / WLC)
